summary: Founding minister of Southold on Long Island, born at Reydon in Suffolk; placed as John's 11th-great-grandfather, though the Youngs descent is unproven.
bio:
The Rev. John Youngs, whose name was also spelled Yonges, was born on 13 November 1598 at Reydon, Suffolk, England, and became the founding minister of Southold, Long Island; William Wells was its leading founder after him. His sister married William Browne of Salem. He married three times: first Joan Herrington at Southwold on 25 July 1622, under a licence for which Mr. Christopher Yonges gave bond; second Joan (Harris), widow of Richard Palgrave; and third Mary (Warren), widow Gardner, who died at Southold in 1678. His children were John, Thomas, Mary, who married Edward Petty, Rachel, Joseph, Benjamin and Christopher.

He died at Southold on 24 February 1671/2, aged 74, and lies under an altar tomb inscribed "Mr Iohn Yongs Minister of the Word and First Setler of the Chvrch of Christ in Sovth Hovld". He is placed as John's 11th-great-grandfather, but the descent is unproven: none of his daughters married William Wells, and the Youngs connection to the Wells family came instead through Mary Wells's daughter Mary, who married a John Youngs. Col. John Youngs and the Youngs family of Oyster Bay are likewise not proven kin.

researchNotes:
Southold's founding minister (William Wells was its leading founder after him). Wives per Youngs (1907): Joan Herrington, Joan (Harris) Palgrave, Mary (Warren) Gardner. Children: John, Thomas, Mary (m. Edward Petty), Rachel, Joseph, Benjamin, Christopher. His sister married William Browne of Salem. Not in the Rootsweb Youngs index as father of a Mary Wells. Col. John Youngs and the Oyster Bay Youngses are therefore not proven kin.

Youngs Family (1907) prints the inscription on Rev. John Youngs's altar tomb: 'Mr Iohn Yongs Minister of the Word and First Setler of the Chvrch of Christ in Sovth Hovld ... Deceased the 24 of Febrvary ... 1671/2 and of His Age 74' ([R4-S1]). It gives his marriages as (1) Joan Herrington at Southwold, 25 July 1622 (license of 24 July 1622, bond by Mr. Christopher Yongs), (2) Joan (Harris), widow of Richard Palgrave, and (3) Mary (Warren), widow Gardner, who died at Southold in 1678. His children were John, Thomas, Mary (m. Edward Petty), Rachel, Joseph, Benjamin and Christopher. No daughter married William Wells ([R4-S1]). The deed of gift of Mary Mapes (formerly Wells), 1678, shows that the Youngs link to the Wells family came through Mary Wells's daughter Mary, who married a John Youngs ([R4-S2]). He is therefore not an ancestor on present evidence.
